newsitem.title: GERMANY: Frankfurt rally to go ahead despite bid withdrawal.
newsitem.headline: Frankfurt rally to go ahead despite bid withdrawal.

text.p: Thyssen AG's works council said it still planned to go ahead with its demonstration in Frankfurt on Tuesday despite the announcement late on Monday that Krupp AG has withdrawn its takeover bid for Thyssen.
"We have reached a partial success but will nevertheless demonstrate," Thyssen group works council chairman Georg Bongen told Reuters.
Bongen said the demonstration, which 30,000 Thyssen workers are expected to attend, was intended as a signal against the "Americanisation" of German society.

Engineering union IG Metall called the demonstration in Frankfurt to protest at the role of banks in advising Krupp on the takeover bid which had sparked fears of heavy job losses at both steelmakers.
Fried. Krupp AG Hoesch-Krupp and Thyssen AG said in a joint statement the companies were exploring cooperation which goes beyond a merger of steel activities.
Krupp said its takeover bid was now void and would not be renewed in future.

The two sides have been in talks since last Thursday over a steel merger after Krupp suspended its cash bid which valued Thyssen at 435 marks ($257) a share, a 25 percent premium to the market when it was made at the beginning of last week.
